candidate_claims.text: The sham threat condition did not significantly change response bias or sensitivity in either task. State anxiety was higher, while overall symptom experience did not significantly differ between the instruction groups.

proof.native_title: Exposure to radiofrequency electromagnetic fields: Comparison of exposimeters with a novel body-worn distributed meter.

candidate_claims.text: Commercial exposimeters generally read lower than the distributed body-worn meter, while ranking total and downlink environments similarly. Agreement varied by frequency band, so similar ranking does not establish identical absolute exposure.
candidate_claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 4 to 6, Results, Discussion and Conclusion

candidate_claims.text: Comparisons use overlapping device bands and assistants who were not using their own phones. Body shielding, calibration, crosstalk and device availability limit interpretation; the measurements do not represent own-phone absorbed dose or average population exposure.
candidate_claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 3 to 6, measurement protocol and limitations

proof.native_title: In‐Situ Measurements of Radiofrequency Electromagnetic Fields Measurements Around 5G Macro Base Stations in the UK

candidate_claims.text: The sampled and extrapolated scenarios were within the public reference levels used by the authors. Background, streaming, speed tests and extrapolation describe different network conditions rather than interchangeable measurements of personal absorbed dose.
candidate_claims.locator: Main PDF physical pages 2 to 4, Methods; pages 7 to 8, Discussion and Conclusions
